name: Reviewers.com
summary: Shopify app that gets video reviews from real US shoppers who order your product with a free code, with a free first campaign of up to 10 videos.
best_for: Shopify brands that want video reviews from US shoppers and are ready to give the product away
skip_if: most of your customers are outside the United States, or you want reviews only from your own buyers
honest_knock: Reviewers are limited to the US, and you pay for each product and its shipping on top of the campaign fee. A campaign needs at least 15 units in stock. The fee works out to about $15 per item at $150 for 10, and more per received video if some reviewers never post. We stopped before submitting, so we could not check video quality or how many reviewers deliver.

Bundles: 5 campaigns (up to 50 items) $750, 5% off, $142.50 each; 10 campaigns (up to 100) $1,500, 10% off, $135 each; 15 campaigns (up to 150) $2,250, 15% off, $127.50 each; 20 campaigns (up to 200) $3,000, 20% off, $120 each; Unlimited $5,000 a month. sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 19 November 2026 on a Shopify development store, with the interface in English. We installed the app, switched on its theme embed and went through the seven step wizard for the free campaign up to the last screen. We did not submit the campaign, so no reviewer ordered or filmed anything, and we paid nothing.
findings: Install: no payment screen appeared. The permission screen asked to view customer and staff data and to edit customers, products, orders, discounts and the Online Store. The wizard was ready about 2 minutes after install.
Setup: campaigns stay locked until the Reviewers core script is switched on in the theme editor and saved. After that the app showed the embed as active.

Wizard: step 1 picks the product and the number of items to give away, 10 by default, and lists only products with at least 15 units in stock. Step 2 sets age range and gender, and the reviewer location is fixed to the US. Later steps set the request timing and optional screening questions and a brief of up to 750 characters.
Last screen: the summary showed 10 items, women 18 to 65 in the US, a review request 7 days after fulfillment, and the billing line Free. We did not press Submit for approval.

How reviewers get the product: they order it from your store with a free discount code that includes shipping, and you process the order like any other. You pay for the product and the shipping yourself.
Plans: the app listing shows a free first campaign of up to 10 videos and 1 campaign a month at $150. Inside the app of our development store the plan screen said no plans were available.
